what_this_found: 21 fixtures in this tree call importorskip, which makes the skip as broad as the widest dependency of anything in their file rather than what the tests beneath them use. Of the 13 fixture-and-module pairs this environment can decide, 0 switch off tests that never touch the module through the measured path, 0 tests in total. Another 15 pairs are explicitly not fully measured.
what_it_costs_today: 0 of those 0 are costing coverage in CI now. CI installs the modules the others are gated on, so those tests run today and go quiet the moment one of those dependencies moves.
where_this_came_from: A review lane found two tests switched off everywhere by this pattern in PR 1011: the fixture they shared asked for Open3D to satisfy a module-scope import that only the harness's main() needed, and CI installs no Open3D. One of the two was the test validating that change's own headline reading. Blocking the import the way real absence does, that file went from 20 passed and 2 skipped to 23 passed. That site is fixed in its own branch; this measures how far the shape reaches.
what_this_does_not_establish: Not that the tests are good, only that the measured path runs. Not that a module is unused by the file -- several of these fixtures sit beside tests that do need the dependency, which is why the measurement is per test rather than per file. And not a complete census: a pair this environment cannot decide is reported as undecided, not as clean.
what_this_measures: Whether a test skipped for a missing module runs when only its fixture's importorskip is bypassed while the module remains genuinely absent. Downstream imports still fail, so import-only dependencies are classified as required rather than as unnecessary skips.
sentinel_overcount_limit: An earlier version of this file said 'provably never touched it'. That is stronger than the instrument can support, and a reviewer demonstrated it rather than arguing it: the fixture sentinel raises AssertionError, so a test that reads it inside `except Exception` can swallow the complaint and pass. The row records broad handlers found in the test file, but this is not a downstream call-graph analysis. Findings therefore establish the observed bypass behaviour, not that no downstream code touched a value.
why_test_identity_and_not_a_count_delta: The first version of this sweep classified a row by bypassed_passed - absent_passed. That counts any test moving into passing, while the criterion is narrower: a test that *skipped* and then passed. A reviewer reproduced the counts exactly, took per-test identities, and found the single test behind the torch finding was FAILED under absence and PASSED under the old poison method -- never skipped, so never switched off by a skip. The same delta can also hide a finding by netting a rise against a drop; they measured ten of the thirteen rows with that capacity and found none, so it was real in principle and had cost nothing in practice. Both are now measured by intersecting sets of test identities, and every row publishes what the delta would have said so the two can be compared.
how_bypass_outcomes_are_interpreted: The target stays genuinely absent. A gated pass shows the fixture skip was unnecessary; a gated failure or error shows the dependency is required; a continued skip is undecided. Unexecuted tests and collection-only outcomes are not classified as justified.

how_to_reproduce_this.needs_a_real_checkout: The sweep refuses to run outside a git checkout, because it resolves the repository root by walking up for .git and its findings are per-file. An exported archive has no repository marker, so the evidence cannot be regenerated from one. A reviewer hit this and reported it as their own plumbing rather than a defect here; recorded so the next one does not have to discover it. No failure count is quoted because the number depends on the environment and neither of us can reproduce it.
how_to_reproduce_this.interpreter_contract: Set PYTHON to the environment under test. Child pytest runs use that interpreter's sys.executable; no checkout-local virtualenv path is required.
how_to_reproduce_this.runtime: about three minutes, two pytest runs per fixture-and-module pair
